articles.body: 전례 없는 통화 팽창과 소비자 물가 지수 상승이 특징인 시대에, 비트코인이 '디지털 금'이자 강력한 인플레이션 헤지 수단이라는 이야기는 상당한 공감을 얻었다. 지지자들은 비트코인이 2,100만 개로 한정된 공급량, 중앙은행의 개입으로부터 자유로운 탈중앙화된 본질, 그리고 가치 하락하는 법정화폐 시대의 안전한 가치 저장 수단이라는 점을 강하게 내세우곤 했다. 이러한 관점은 코로나19 팬데믹에 대응하여 전 세계 중앙은행들이 단행한 광범위한 양적완화 조치 이후 특히 설득력을 얻었으며, 이는 통화 가치 하락과 임박한 인플레이션 환경에 대한 우려를 증폭시켰다. 많은 이들은 비트코인이 경제적 불확실성 시기에 구매력을 보존할 수 있는, 금과 같은 전통적인 안전자산의 현대적이고 기술적으로 우월한 대안을 제공한다고 믿었다. 그러나 최근의 인플레이션 주기와 시장 스트레스 시기 동안 비트코인의 성과를 데이터 기반으로 엄밀하게 검토해 보면, 더 복잡하고 종종 모순되는 현실이 드러난다. 인플레이션 헤지로서의 이론적 근거는 어느 정도 타당성을 가지지만, 실제 적용과 역사적 행동은 상당한 한계를 보여준다. 이 칼럼은 이러한 제약들을 비판적으로 분석하여, 지배적인 서사를 넘어 비트코인이 현재 일관되고 강력한 인플레이션 헤지 역할을 안정적으로 수행하는 것을 방해하는 근본적인 문제들을 탐구하고자 한다.

articles.title: The Nuanced Reality: Deconstructing Bitcoin's Limitations as an Inflation Hedge
articles.excerpt: Introduction The narrative of Bitcoin as "digital gold" and a potent hedge against inflation has gained significant traction, particularly in an era characterized by unprecedented monetary expansion a…
articles.body: Introduction The narrative of Bitcoin as "digital gold" and a potent hedge against inflation has gained significant traction, particularly in an era characterized by unprecedented monetary expansion and rising consumer price indices. Proponents often highlight Bitcoin's finite supply cap of 21 million coins, its decentralized nature immune to central bank manipulation, and its perceived status as a store of value in a world of depreciating fiat currencies. This perspective became particularly compelling following the extensive quantitative easing measures enacted by central banks globally in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, which fueled concerns about currency debasement and a looming inflationary environment.
articles.author: Juno Kim

articles.title: Sorry, That Was For Another Chat
articles.excerpt: You have done this. There is something in your clipboard that belonged to a different conversation — you copied it for another reason, or you forgot it was there at all — and it ends up pasted into a…
articles.body: You have done this. There is something in your clipboard that belonged to a different conversation — you copied it for another reason, or you forgot it was there at all — and it ends up pasted into a chat where it makes no sense. Most of the time you catch it before sending. Sometimes you don't. There is a newer version of the same mistake, and if you work with agents you have lived it this week: twenty sessions open in parallel, each one waiting on something, and you answer the wrong one. The reply was true — just not there. I was setting up an experiment about exactly this when it happened to me. An agent had just put an API key on my clipboard, and in the same breath suggested a shell command to save it. I copied the command to run it. The command overwrote the key.

articles.title: Chapter 9 — Route Async Inputs Through One Service-Owned Pipeline
articles.excerpt: What changes when the same feature receives its data four different ways: during hydration, from a Promise, through an Observable, and from an Angular HTTP Resource? The source contracts look differen…
articles.body: What changes when the same feature receives its data four different ways: during hydration, from a Promise, through an Observable, and from an Angular HTTP Resource? The source contracts look different enough to invite separate loading, error, and state-management paths. This chapter follows each one to the same service-owned FeatureCell™ boundary, where the more important question is revealed: who still owns the result when the source succeeds, stalls, or fails? The component supplies teaching controls and presentation state. The service registers the source and chooses the appropriate state API. The pipeline resolves the input, applies the existing filters and reducers, tracks loading and errors, and commits the resulting State. The source changes; the ownership boundary does not.

articles.title: The Court Order Behind C#: How Two Keywords Started a New Language
articles.excerpt: On November 17th, 1998, a federal judge in San Jose gave Microsoft ninety days to change its Java tools. The court papers in that case talk about two words that C# developers still type every day: del…
articles.body: On November 17th, 1998, a federal judge in San Jose gave Microsoft ninety days to change its Java tools. The court papers in that case talk about two words that C# developers still type every day: delegate and multicast . This is the story of how a lawsuit over Java ended up producing C#. It's told from the court records, the documents the companies published at the time, and what C#'s lead designer, Anders Hejlsberg, has said in public. The man from Borland In the early eighties, Anders Hejlsberg wrote a small, very fast Pascal compiler. Borland sold it as Turbo Pascal. Later, at Borland, he led the team that designed Delphi. In Delphi you drew a window, dropped a button on it, and wrote the code that should run on click. Keep that button in mind.

articles.title: OpenAI agents tried to hack Wikipedia tools and flooded it with traffic
articles.excerpt: The reports of OpenAI agents harming 3rd party sites keep coming.
articles.body: The publisher of Wikipedia said Monday that OpenAI agents attempted to hack a note-taking tool it hosts, made unauthorized edits, and sent millions of resource-intensive requests to its infrastructure, in the latest instance of OpenAI systems taking harmful and potentially dangerous actions. The objective of some of the OpenAI agents’ actions, the Wikimedia Foundation said , was to use Wikipedia as a proxy for fetching data from third-party sites. In one case, the agents posted “malicious edits” that were intended to repurpose a citation tool as a proxy. In another, the agents made unsuccessful attempts to compromise the Wikipedia Etherpad note-taking tool so it would serve the same purpose.
articles.author: Dan Goodin
